Subject: Operator witnessing & chain-of-custody for on-prem deployment — MSA/OrderForm redlines

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — we are ready to move forward on the dedicated on-prem deployment but procurement needs a few things clarified before we sign the order form (OF-7789). Specifically MedSys's security team has asked for: 

- A formal operator witnessing process (defined window and observer roles)
- Chain-of-custody / signed snapshot proof for the operator handover (checksums, manifest)
- Retention and exportability of audit logs (for our internal auditors)
- A contingency snapshot deposit (escrow-like) if Redwood cannot recover operator access in an incident

Can you point me to the contract language you would accept (MSA addendum + Order Form exhibit) or share redlines? We need to include the language in our purchase packet by Friday 6/4.

Order form: OF-7789
Primary contact for procurement: Claire Evans (cc'd)
Security lead: Rajiv Patel, Director of IT, MedSys

Thanks — if it's easier we can schedule a short call to walk through.

Regards,
Rajiv

Subject: Re: Operator witnessing & chain-of-custody for on-prem deployment — MSA / Order Form coordination

Rajiv — thanks, appreciate the clear list. High level: we can support a short, auditable operator witnessing workflow and an optional snapshot deposit process. Attached are two working artifacts to start the contract conversation: 1) draft_operator_witnessing_addendum.pdf (proposed addendum language and flow) and 2) witnessing_checklist.xlsx (technical checklist + witness log template).

Proposed minimal scope (for the addendum / Order Form exhibit):
- Witnessing window: mutually scheduled 2-hour window with Redwood observer + MedSys observer
- Deliverable: signed manifest (SHA256 checksums) + notarized transfer statement (digital signature ok)
- Audit logs: 90 days default retention (extendable via addendum) with export format (JSON, gzip)
- Snapshot deposit: optional: encrypted image stored with a 3rd-party custodian for 180 days; release conditions defined in addendum

Timeline we can hit:
- Internal review + redline: 48–72 hours
- Final addendum for legal review: by EOD 6/3
- DocuSign-ready by 6/4 if procurement signs off on scope/cost

Open items for you:
- Does MedSys require the deposit to be in-scope for our standard SOW or billed as a one-time professional service?
- Any compliance-specific formatting for audit log exports? (fields required)

I'll loop Legal and Eng (added Priyom) to capture concrete redlines and the cost impact. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call — suggest 6/2 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator witnessing & chain-of-custody for on-prem deployment — technical clarifications

Thanks — quick technical follow-ups to make sure the addendum covers what we need for a smooth handover: 

1) Access path during witnessing: do you want Redwood to operate behind our console (we'll provide a read-only observer) or to run operations from a Redwood-maintained bastion with MedSys observers connected? We can support either, but contract wording differs.

2) Snapshot proof: our standard approach is an S3 manifest with per-file SHA256 and a signed manifest.json (PKI signature). We can include a signed timestamp (RFC 3161) as evidence. Would MedSys accept a PKI-signed manifest and sha256 per-file checksums?

3) Operator identity & scope: propose we enumerate operator accounts in Exhibit B and restrict actions to the exact runbook steps listed in the witnessing_checklist.xlsx.

4) Escrow/custodian: if MedSys requires a 3rd-party custodian we can suggest two vendors we have used; custodial storage will be billed as a one-time service + monthly storage.

If procurement prefers to avoid a third party, we can include a conditional paragraph that triggers an encrypted snapshot transfer to MedSys upon failed remediation within a defined SLA window.

I'll incorporate these technical specifics into the legal redline once we agree on the access model and snapshot proof format.

— Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Operator witnessing & chain-of-custody for on-prem deployment — proposed redline language

Rajiv / team — attaching a working redline (MSA_redline_operator_addendum.docx) with suggested contract text. Key commercial/legal points summarized below: 

- Operator Witnessing Addendum: adds Exhibit C to the Order Form that defines witness windows, roles, and the signed-manifest requirement.
- Snapshot Custody: two options: (1) Redwood holds encrypted snapshot with 3rd-party custodian for a defined hold period (recommended); (2) Encrypted transfer to MedSys on remediation failure (requires inspection protocol and acceptance criteria).
- Audit logs: default 90-day retention; MedSys may request extended retention as a separately billable service.
- Liability cap carve-out: limited carve-out for evidence delivery obligations (we cannot accept open-ended liability for third-party storage events).

Suggested timeline: Legal will accept a redline within 48 hours. Please confirm whether the snapshot deposit will be part of the SOW or a billable add-on so I can include appropriate payment terms.

If MedSys confirms option (1) we will include custodian details and a minimal escrow acceptance test. If (2), we will include acceptance criteria for the transfer (hash checks, transfer logs, transfer receipt signed by both parties).

Happy to take comments on the redline; small edits on language are fine but any substantive program changes (e.g., unlimited custody retention) will need commercial sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: MSA_redline_operator_addendum.docx

All — this looks good and covers the concerns our security team raised. MedSys prefers option (1): encrypted snapshot with 3rd-party custodian for 180 days and a short acceptance test (hash verification + signed manifest). Please include custodian name and cost estimate in the final redline.

We agree to the default 90-day audit log retention for now; we may request an extension during our audit prep window later this year. For billing: treat snapshot custody as a one-time professional service with quarterly storage charges — procurement will include this in the PO.

Please send the final redline and a DocuSign packet. We're on a slightly accelerated sign timeline so if you can get us DocuSign by Monday 6/7 that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Rajiv
